question: Should Discord source-message subagent progress become a permanent OpenClaw feature using this new configuration and plugin-lifecycle contract, or should it be narrowed around an existing/shared lifecycle seam before landing?
rationale: The UX is proven, but repository policy makes new configuration and plugin API surfaces compatibility-sensitive, and the correct ownership boundary cannot be selected safely without Discord and subagent maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow around one lifecycle seam
options.body: Approve the UX but consolidate it with yielded-parent progress, minimize public configuration/API additions, and require a clean rebase plus refreshed proof before merge.

options.title: Accept the current contract
options.body: Treat the seven configuration leaves, requester message metadata, channel lifecycle adapter, and persisted cleanup marker as supported permanent contracts after conflict resolution and upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause for lifecycle consolidation
options.body: Hold this PR until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95996 establishes the canonical parent/subagent lifecycle, then rebase or replace this branch against that seam.

recommendation.title: Narrow around one lifecycle seam
recommendation.body: Approve the UX but consolidate it with yielded-parent progress, minimize public configuration/API additions, and require a clean rebase plus refreshed proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily defines Discord user-facing reaction behavior and Discord configuration, with @tyler6204 needed for the shared subagent lifecycle boundary.
